prompt.context:
Our client is Great Burger (GB), a fast food chain that competes head-to-head with McDonald's, Wendy's, Burger King, KFC, and similar chains. GB is the fourth largest fast food chain worldwide by number of stores in operation. GB offers food and combos for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. GB owns some stores but operates primarily under a franchising model, with 85% of stores owned by franchisees who pay a franchise fee to GB while GB controls major business decisions such as menu and store appearance.

As part of its growth strategy, GB has analyzed potential acquisition targets including Heavenly Donuts (HD), a growing doughnut producer with both US and international store presence. HD also operates under a franchising model, but differently: while GB franchises individual restaurants, HD franchises areas or regions in which franchisees are required to open a certain number of stores.

GB's CEO has hired McKinsey to advise on whether GB should acquire HD.
prompt.question: Should GB acquire Heavenly Donuts? The case will explore this question across several dimensions including strategic rationale, synergies, market sizing, and profitability analysis.

clarifying_info.q: What is GB's primary motivation for considering this acquisition?
clarifying_info.a: Growth strategy — GB is looking for acquisition targets and HD is one candidate being evaluated.

clarifying_info.q: Does GB have experience with acquisitions?
clarifying_info.a: That is one of the areas you should explore as part of your analysis.

clarifying_info.q: What is the timeline for the decision?
clarifying_info.a: No specific timeline is given; focus on whether GB should acquire HD and under what conditions.

exhibits.title: GB and HD Store and Financial Comparison
exhibits.shows: A side-by-side comparison of GB and HD on store counts by region, annual store growth rates, financial metrics (total store sales, parent company revenues, key expenses as % of sales, profit as % of sales, and sales per store), and industry average sales per store.

exhibits.title: Sales and Profitability per Store
exhibits.shows: Per-store unit economics for GB stores and hypothetical HD doughnut sales within GB stores, including units sold, price per unit, margin percentages, and the cannibalization rate of HD products on GB products.

framework: Stand-alone value of HD: Assess HD's market attractiveness (doughnut market growth, HD's historical and projected sales growth broken into store count growth and same-store sales growth), competitive landscape (other major national chains, relative growth/profit), HD's profitability and margins, and capital required to fund HD's growth (store capex, working capital).

Synergies and strategic fit: Identify cost synergies (corporate SG&A consolidation, purchasing scale on overlapping inputs, leveraging GB's property/equipment cost advantage) and revenue synergies (cross-selling doughnuts in GB stores or GB products in HD stores, using GB's international presence to expand HD globally, leveraging GB's superior store-location skills for new HD openings, faster HD expansion via GB's capital access).
Management team and cultural fit: Evaluate capabilities of HD's top and middle management, assess cultural compatibility, and estimate what percentage of key management could integrate successfully.
GB's M&A capabilities: Review GB's past experience integrating acquisitions and assess the operational challenge of managing two structurally different franchise models simultaneously.

questions.prompt: What areas would you want to explore to determine whether GB should acquire HD?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers four buckets: (1) Stand-alone HD value — market growth, HD revenue/store growth, competition, profitability, and capital needs; (2) Synergies/strategic fit — cost reductions and revenue upside; (3) Management/cultural fit — team quality and integration risk; (4) GB's acquisition capability — track record and ability to manage dual franchise structures. Candidates should not yet dive deep into synergy quantification (that comes in Q2).

questions.prompt: What potential synergies can you think of between GB and HD? (Exhibit 1 is provided)
questions.guidance: Cost synergies: Corporate SG&A consolidation is the biggest opportunity. Some food-cost savings through larger purchasing volume on overlapping items (beverages, frying oil), though ingredient overlap is limited. GB's lower property and equipment cost rate (4.6% vs 8.5%) suggests superior lease-negotiation skills that could be applied to HD. Revenue synergies: Cross-sell doughnuts in GB stores; potentially sell select GB products in HD stores. GB's much larger international footprint (1,500 non-NA stores vs HD's 20) gives GB the knowledge/skills to accelerate HD's international expansion. GB's sales/store ($1.1M) exceeds industry average ($0.9M) while HD's ($0.7M) trails its industry average ($0.8M), suggesting GB may have superior site-selection capabilities to improve new HD store performance. GB's larger size and lower relative debt may provide better and cheaper capital access to fund faster HD store expansion.

questions.prompt: The team thinks synergies can double HD's US market share in 5 years and expand HD store count 2.5x. What sales/store will HD require in 5 years? Assume: doughnut consumption/capita = $10/year today growing to $20/year in 5 years; US population = 300M. Use Exhibit 1 as needed.
questions.guidance: Candidate should size today's HD US market share, project the market forward, apply the doubled-share target, divide by the new store count. A good candidate notes the reasonableness check: the implied sales/store is less than double today's, consistent with per-capita consumption doubling.

math.setup: Step 1: calculate HD's current US market share. Step 2: project total US doughnut market in year 5. Step 3: calculate HD's required sales in year 5 (doubled share applied to larger market). Step 4: divide by new store count.
steps: HD current market share: $700M / $3,000M = 23% → round to 25% (interviewer instruction)
HD required sales in 5 years: 25% x 2 x $6B = $3B
HD current stores (Exhibit 1): 1,000 (NA) used as base; total stores = 1,020 but calculation uses 1,000
math.answer: $1.2M per store. Reasonableness check: this is less than double today's $0.7M/store while per-capita consumption is projected to double — reasonable given that new stores also contribute to total sales growth.

questions.prompt: How would you assess the profitability impact of the synergy of selling doughnuts in GB stores?
questions.guidance: Strong answer covers three layers: (1) Incremental revenue — doughnuts sold per store x price x number of GB stores; (2) Incremental costs — food/production costs, extra staff and training, software changes, marketing and advertising, distribution costs if doughnuts are not produced in-house; (3) Incremental investment — additional store space if new customers are attracted, store layout changes for in-house production. Bonus: candidate proactively raises cannibalization — doughnut sales will cannibalize GB breakfast products more than lunch/dinner; can estimate cannibalization using historical rates from prior new-product launches at GB or by examining how HD store openings near competitors historically affect competitor sales.

questions.prompt: What would be the incremental profit per store if GB sells 50,000 doughnuts per store at $2/unit at 60% margin with a 10% cannibalization rate on GB sales? (Exhibit 2 is provided)
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate HD contribution minus contribution lost from cannibalized GB sales. The cannibalization formula: GB units/store x cannibalization rate x GB price x GB margin = lost profit. If candidate skips Q5, interviewer tells them the answer is $15K incremental profit/store for use in Q6.

math.setup: Incremental profit = (HD revenue contribution per store) minus (cannibalized GB profit per store)
steps: HD contribution: 50,000 units x $2/unit x 60% margin = $60,000
Cannibalized GB sales (units): 300,000 GB units/store x 10% = 30,000 units
Cannibalized GB profit: 30,000 units x $3/unit x 50% margin = $45,000
math.answer: $5,000 incremental profit per store. (Note: the math yields $15K contribution from HD minus $45K lost GB profit = -$30K if formula is misread; the correct arithmetic as stated in the casebook gives $60K - $45K = $15K. The casebook answer is $15K — $5K appears to be a casebook typo or alternative rounding; the stated formula yields $60K - $45K = $15K.)

questions.prompt: Synthesis: You run into GB's CEO in the hall. Summarize McKinsey's perspective so far on whether GB should acquire HD.
questions.guidance: A strong CEO-ready synthesis is structured, top-down, and action-oriented: lead with a directional view, support with 1-2 quantified findings, name what still needs to be done, and close with next steps. Avoid listing every analysis detail — synthesize to the executive level.

brainstorming.prompt: What potential synergies can you think of between GB and HD?

categories.name: Cost synergies
ideas: Consolidate corporate SG&A — biggest opportunity given HD's 15% vs GB's 8% corporate cost ratio
Purchasing scale on overlapping food inputs (beverages, frying oil) to lower cost of sales
Apply GB's superior property and equipment cost management (4.6% vs HD's 8.5%) — likely superior lease-negotiation skills — to HD's real estate portfolio

categories.name: Revenue synergies
ideas: Sell HD doughnuts in GB stores — incremental revenue from captive GB customer base
Sell selected GB products in HD stores
Leverage GB's extensive international footprint (1,500 non-NA stores) to accelerate HD's global expansion beyond its current 20 non-NA stores
Apply GB's superior store-location selection capabilities (GB sales/store $1.1M vs industry $0.9M) when opening new HD locations to close the gap vs HD's current below-average $0.7M/store
Use GB's larger balance sheet and capital market access to fund faster HD store expansion than HD could achieve independently

recommendation: Early findings lead us to believe that acquiring HD would create significant value for GB and that GB should proceed with the acquisition.

Selling HD doughnuts in GB stores alone could add approximately $15K in incremental profit per GB store, implying roughly $50M in incremental profit across North American GB stores where synergies are most immediately actionable.

Additional revenue and cost synergies — including SG&A consolidation, purchasing scale, international expansion, and improved HD store economics — have not yet been fully quantified but appear meaningful based on the structural gap in cost ratios.
risks: Managing two structurally different franchise models simultaneously (individual restaurant franchising vs. area/regional franchising) creates integration complexity.
Cultural misalignment between GB and HD management could impair retention of key HD talent.
Cannibalization of GB breakfast products from in-store doughnut sales reduces net profit uplift.
HD's current below-industry-average sales/store ($0.7M vs $0.8M industry) suggests operational underperformance that GB must address post-acquisition.
HD has minimal international presence outside North America — international expansion will require significant investment and time.
next_steps: Quantify remaining revenue and cost synergies (SG&A consolidation, purchasing savings, international expansion value) to determine a maximum acquisition price GB should be willing to pay.
Develop a post-merger integration plan addressing how to manage dual franchise structures and align corporate cultures.
Conduct management assessment of HD's leadership team to identify retention risks and integration requirements.
Model the full cannibalization impact of in-store doughnut sales across all dayparts to refine the profit-per-store estimate.
